packageRules.description: The shared preset automerges every update type. Here only patch, pin and digest updates keep that; minor and major updates wait for review unless a later rule turns automerge back on for them

Automerge minor updates of these module families: the Kubernetes libraries (k8s.io and controller-runtime, which the shared preset bumps together in one kubernetes group, and a group automerges only when every update in it does), the two Gateway API modules, where TestVendoredGatewayAPIMinorHasBeenAudited still fails a minor the spec audit has not been read against, and the hack/tools code generators, where make verify-generated fails a bump that changes generated output

hack/tools/go.mod pins the code generators and helm-docs through tool directives, and go mod tidy records their modules as indirect requires, which Renovate leaves alone unless it matches them to a tool directive. The controller-gen and helm-docs directives name a package inside the module rather than the module itself, so every tool is enabled explicitly instead of relying on how a directive is matched. A generator bump that changes generated output fails make verify-generated in CI until someone runs make generate on the branch; a helm-docs bump fails the chart README check until someone runs make helm-docs.
Automerge all GitHub Actions updates including major
Allow Renovate to bump go directive in go.mod

cloudflare/cloudflared and quic-go/quic-go are require-only entries shadowed by an unconditional replace with no version on its left side (see go.mod) - a bump of either never reaches the vendored code, so mark it in the PR title itself, not just the body, because a title like 'update ... [security]' on a no-op is worse than no PR at all
prBodyNotes: :warning: **This is a no-op.** The `require` line this PR bumps sits under an unconditional `replace` directive in `go.mod` (no version on its left side) that ignores it - see the `FIXME(#610)` comment there. Merging this changes only the version string in `go.mod`, nothing that actually builds. It is still worth merging as a record that the pin is stale, but it fixes nothing by itself.

packageRules.description: chungthuang/quic-go is the replace target that github.com/quic-go/quic-go's require line above is shadowed by - unlike the require bump, this one changes the vendored code, and can silently undo a deliberate pin (see issue #610's #612 near-miss). Mark it in the PR title as well as the body so it reads differently from the no-op require bump
packageRules.commitMessageSuffix: - moves the actual pin, review by hand (FIXME #610)
prBodyNotes: :warning: **This changes the vendored code.** This module is the target of the `replace github.com/quic-go/quic-go => ...` directive in `go.mod` - see the `FIXME(#610)` comment there. Unlike a bump of the `require` line above that replace, this one takes effect, and can silently undo a deliberate pin chosen to match what cloudflared itself requires. Verify against that comment before merging.

packageRules.description: github.com/lexfrei/cloudflared is our cloudflared fork; its replace-target pin moves by hand through a deliberate rebase (CLAUDE.md 'Cloudflared Fork' section), never through Renovate
Renovate ships several releases a day; the image pinned in renovate-config.yaml only runs the config validator, so batch its bumps weekly

Keep the two Gateway API modules and every doc site that names their versions in one PR. Split across PRs each branch is red on its own: a gomod bump alone leaves the pinned docs stale, and a docs bump alone claims a version the vendored module is not on

customManagers.description: Update Go version in GitHub Actions

Update digest-pinned tool images in GitHub Actions workflows. The tag is there for humans; the digest is what docker resolves, so both have to move together and a single matchString keeps them in step
Update versioned binaries in GitHub Actions workflows, both the SOMETHING_VERSION="..." shell form and an action's version: input

Update the Gateway API bundle version wherever a doc or script names it. internal/docsdrift/gatewayapiversiondoc_test.go asserts every one of these against consts.BundleVersion in the vendored module, so a gomod bump that leaves them behind fails CI - grouped with the gomod dep by the packageRules entry above so they move in one PR. The go datasource is deliberate: it is the same version stream the gomod manager resolves, whereas repo releases are a separate stream that can list a tag the module proxy does not serve

Update the conformance suite version CLAUDE.md names. sigs.k8s.io/gateway-api/conformance is a nested module with its own release stream, tagged conformance/vX.Y.Z rather than vX.Y.Z, and internal/docsdrift/conformanceversiondoc_test.go compares this claim to that module's require entry in go.mod - so it tracks the module, not the repo's releases
